note: Fleet default routing. Per-workspace loop-config.json `harness.roles` overrides by role/mode, role, or default. Four deployments only. Astra plans and nothing else: `planner` is the one role on gpt-6-astra, and it emits a JSON plan, never code. Grok (grok-4-6) writes the code: it holds `researcher`, the only role that authors and runs experiments. Everything else is split between the two DeepSeek lines. deepseek-v4-pro takes the judgement roles that read a whole transcript (critic, verifier, surgeon, synthesizer, refine_proposer, and the `default`); deepseek-v4-flash takes the short structured roles (explorer, budget_planner, steward, probe, frontier, narrowness_critic, adoption_critic). Researcher and its reviewers sit on different publishers (xAI vs DeepSeek), so `Router.check`'s independence gate is mechanical. Astra lives on the resource's openai.azure.com host over the v1 Responses route (function tools with reasoning are refused on chat completions); Grok and DeepSeek are served on the services.ai.azure.com host over the Foundry model-inference route. Set AZURE_OPENAI_ENDPOINT and AZURE_AI_ENDPOINT in /etc/adv-loop/env.d/harness. A session cannot start on a model whose price is unknown. `architecture_tier` sizes the system reference each alias receives (core, lean, role): deepseek-flash is `lean`, the three others `role`; no alias ships at `core` because every role that touches the sandbox needs the tools and sandbox chapters. `context_window` is the pre-flight size guard: an API-billed session cannot start on a model without one, and the values shipped here are placeholders until each deployment's model card is checked. Budgets carry the reference's share: default 17.5, critic 11, refine_proposer 2.5.
